TargetEndpoint: Egg laying-to-hatch interval and cohort mean conditional on observed hatch
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: B06 Table 2 p. 169 reports 16.7 d and 15.7 d near 24.7 C for separate founder populations.
MappingToCurrentParameter: Elapsed egg progress maps to a fixed conditional cohort mean in one admitted regime. Full hatch incidence and individual variability are separate.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Days times 86400000 to integer ms. Retain actual stage temperature, rounding and nesting. A fixed-regime mean is the stated approximation.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Independently defined clock only under measured stage entry, regime and hatch conditioning. Realized hatch competes with reserve depletion.
ProposedTreatment: Use a host-resolved constant timer as an opt-in assay. Keep both exposed population references and the frozen fixture.
RangeBasis: Use the matched published estimate and its reported uncertainty and recording resolution. Use St. Petersburg as a separate sensitivity context. Leave unobserved regimes unset.

TargetEndpoint: Landmark-to-landmark larval and prepupal/pupal duration and incidence of completing each stage
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: B06 reports larval and combined prepupal plus pupal times. B01 first observed worker includes time from flight. B07 colony counts do not isolate juvenile timings.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The larval software timer starts after a tissue gate. Prepupal observations cannot isolate the existing Pupa timer.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Use interval-censored multistate timing with observed landmarks, nutrition state and temperature. Convert stage elapsed days only after mapping start/end.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Elapsed time mixes acquisition, nutritional eligibility, stage progress and death.
ProposedTreatment: Measure linked juvenile state and feeding. Keep combined prepupal/pupal observables until stage boundaries are identifiable.
RangeBasis: Use reported stage durations and nonprogression as contextual bounds. Derive separate timing ranges from matched active conditions, without cold extrapolation.

TargetEndpoint: Resting or basal whole-animal power by caste, age, body mass and condition
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: N27 Clark setup gives focal whole-individual queen and worker oxygen scales. B04 is mass-normalized and B05 adult females are sexual-stage observations.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The inherited basal field is shared across stages under a lineage configuration. The published cohorts do not identify that shared scalar.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: 1 nJ/ms equals 1 uW. Conditional conversion from uL O2/h uses J/mL O2 divided by 3.6, with respiratory substrate uncertainty.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Separate body mass, caste, instrument and stage; apparent fit from survival can trade basal cost against reserves and intake.
ProposedTreatment: Measure target cohorts or document an admitted resting proxy before fitting a cohort-specific rate.
RangeBasis: Use matched respiration repeats and conversion uncertainty. Keep published comparator scales and fixture values separate.

TargetEndpoint: Incremental energy expenditure during timed actual activity above matched resting power
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Respiration and ethogram studies have separate observation units and activity definitions. Program residence has no measured power increment.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The source adds a fixed cost to selected adult roles, including waiting within those roles.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Use time-integrated measured activity increments at fixed body mass, temperature and cohort. Convert matched energy flux to nJ/ms.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Role dwell, observed active time and resting cost compensate when only total depletion is measured.
ProposedTreatment: Record disjoint completed activity intervals and paired rest/activity measurements before estimating any premium.
RangeBasis: Derive intervals from observed per-act or bout repeatability and measured baseline power. No numerical increment from role scans.

TargetEndpoint: Water-mass change per elapsed time at measured temperature and humidity
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Desiccation survival and water-access rearing give exposure and outcome. They do not measure the model's body-water flux.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The configured integer loss and its period represent a rate. The period is a numerical choice.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Measure water mass over time by stage, caste and condition. Convert matched rate to ug per fixed configured interval with documented rounding.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Survival confounds initial hydration, usable capacity, loss and uptake.
ProposedTreatment: Observe body-water change and intake separately. Keep numerical remainder and loss cadence in the engineering test.
RangeBasis: Derive a rate interval from repeated measured flux at matched exposures. Do not infer it from a fatality count.

TargetEndpoint: Component-specific transfer from crop to body over time after a known delivered dose
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Oral contacts, meal size, whole-colony growth and congener isotope allocation give context. None provides focal crop-to-body flux and latency by component.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The configured rates cap a pulse and may be inactive under crop or headroom limits. A known gift does not measure absorbed mass.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Measure a time series of crop and retained/used components under a known dose. Compare conserved delay or uptake kinetics before converting to ug/s.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Pulse period, uptake rate, capacity, yield, stage and starting reserves can produce the same total uptake.
ProposedTreatment: Isolate delivery, dose and uptake. Fit only a rate visible under matched and informative conditions.
RangeBasis: Use observed uptake slopes and saturation by component and stage. Before those data report sensitivity over declared physical bounds without biological estimates.

TargetEndpoint: Caste- and condition-specific maximum retained crop mass or usable hydrated body mass
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: N01 meal size is a single intake endpoint. Oral contacts and survival under desiccation supply no saturation or retention estimate.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The configured cap is a separate compartment bound. Body hydration and crop fluid are distinct.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Measure maximum or saturation curves in mass units, with measured density if converting fluid volume and body-water definition declared.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Cap and dose/rate cannot be separated when no observed subject approaches saturation.
ProposedTreatment: Obtain component and saturation observations before calibrating; record cohort and body-size effects.
RangeBasis: Use physiological compartment measurements and cohort variation. Keep lower observations as lower bounds and do not treat them as measured maxima.

TargetEndpoint: Per-egg component export and usable initial energy for viable first-worker eggs by founder condition
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Founding counts and tissue histolysis constrain output and reserve change. Sexual-stage calorimetry does not supply first-worker egg component export or usable energy.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The code debits mother and credits offspring with protein, water or usable energy. Separate these terms from maternal dissipation.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Measure egg composition and maternal/body balance at laying. Any conversion from chemical to usable energy requires a declared physiological model.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Egg export, reserve utilization, maintenance and reproduction attempt censoring are coupled in viable brood counts.
ProposedTreatment: Constrain independent export measurements first. Fit an effective offspring budget only if an observable compartment mapping exists.
RangeBasis: Use measured per-egg composition and viable cohort condition intervals. Retain uncertainty on energy use and avoid sexual-stage substitution.

TargetEndpoint: Act-specific unloaded trajectory speed by caste and assay condition
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Flat-canvas workers give path and chord speeds. B02 retrieved counts and time markers do not give caste-specific unloaded trajectories.
MappingToCurrentParameter: Care motion scalar applies to timed segments and differs from free search or chord speed.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Use path length per observed segment time in m/s. Align observation cadence, load state, geometry and running conditions.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Speed, non-movement waits and coverage trade off in time-to-retrieval. B2-F01/F03 shared tracks provide one lineage for the overlapping subset.
ProposedTreatment: Measure unloaded segments during actual care for target castes and independent groups.
RangeBasis: Use matched segment distributions and tracked accuracy. Treat flat-canvas values as contextual bounds.

TargetEndpoint: Travel speed during verified brood custody by caste, load and path
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: R1C Table II/IV derived 11.75–29.89 mm/s across twelve repeated normal-light returns from two trained workers. B02 first-retrieving markers are a different endpoint.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The source gives a descriptive worker scale in a trained apparatus. It does not give matched queen speed or a universal load-dependent scalar.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Convert mm/s to m/s by division by 1000. Use actual path time and distinguish handling and stationary periods.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Retrieval counts confound handling latency, speed and route. Repeated runs within workers do not identify population variance.
ProposedTreatment: Obtain timed matched trajectories with observed load and caste and group nesting.
RangeBasis: Use R1C scale as a sensitivity check with source conditions. Base empirical intervals on independent matched paths.

TargetEndpoint: Act-specific duration from annotated onset to completion or interruption
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Scans and first-retrieving markers lack aligned event start/end for these components. R1L supports conditional behavior context.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The timed phases commit separate observable actions. Assigning the same first marker to all phases would confound elapsed care and transport.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Score video intervals at declared cadence and compare censor-aware duration distributions in ms. Use a specified fixed approximation only after measurement.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Selection, waiting, contact and travel are separate from act duration.
ProposedTreatment: Acquire event-annotated independent data. Retain unsuccessful and interrupted acts.
RangeBasis: Use recording resolution and matched bout variability. Initial sensitivity bounds require explicit apparatus and workflow assumptions.

TargetEndpoint: Duration of completed eligible worker contact during a defined care-access manipulation
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: B01 access contrasts do not time every worker contact. Worker-worker oral bout duration has a separate definition.
MappingToCurrentParameter: A prior contact gate is not a measured duration for all worker or queen interactions.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Score contact onset, offset and eligibility with observed stage and cadence. Fit conditional duration in ms.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Contact detection, windowing and memory can compensate for a wrong duration in observed scan fractions.
ProposedTreatment: Observe marked worker contacts before estimating a care contact timer.
RangeBasis: Use matched contact durations and observation error. Keep oral-bout durations contextual.

TargetEndpoint: Carried load limit and realized load by cohort, material and transport mode
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Meal size and placement observations report realized loads or acts. They do not measure maximum capacity of all worker cohorts.
MappingToCurrentParameter: Seed and inherited capacities are generic caps. Intake, body size and destination limit realized carried load independently.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Compare measured component mass or volume with stated density, load type and posture. Fit capacity only when observed exposure tests the cap.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Realized load cannot separate scarcity, choice and capacity unless matched treatments reach the bound.
ProposedTreatment: Collect paired load and condition measurements. Keep observed loads separate from guaranteed capacities.
RangeBasis: Use measured loads as lower bounds on support and observed saturation and mass ranges for upper bounds.

TargetEndpoint: Actual excavation work time and incremental energetic cost per specified removed volume and material
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Group excavation and pellet observations give trajectories and material effects. Rest-context respiration does not give digging cost.
MappingToCurrentParameter: Configured duration and quantum cost need a defined work unit and contact/task context.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Measure time, volume, and activity-related cost above matched rest. Convert physical volume with the declared quantum size cubed.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Group initiation and transport effort can trade against per-act duration or debit in final void volume.
ProposedTreatment: Separate work, pickup and deposit times and energy. Keep quantization a fidelity control.
RangeBasis: Use matched substrate and volume observations, including no work and failure; bound energetic increments from repeated measurements.

TargetEndpoint: Contrast between available private and trail cues for choices and completed returns
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Experiments manipulate cue and experience. The flags select explicit software treatments.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The flag chooses a model path. Conditional response is the biological comparison.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Report labeled on/off interventions and use measured exposures and route outcomes.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Without single-cue and both-cue controls, experience and marking can compensate.
ProposedTreatment: Fix each flag per declared treatment and validate cue combinations.
RangeBasis: Use the prespecified categorical arms and admissible cue exposure. Do not derive a fitted probability for a flag.

TargetEndpoint: Actual care, retrieval and overlapping work under selected implementation contracts
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Observed care and retrieval constrain outputs. The modes choose which software capability is being exercised.
MappingToCurrentParameter: An implementation selector does not identify a biological probability, duration or priority.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Keep each mode and its observables explicit in comparisons.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Motor choice, process ownership and care time affect counts and latency.
ProposedTreatment: Freeze the mode before evaluating results; retain current fixture and motion controls.
RangeBasis: Compare declared modes with matched handling and transport exposure; measure resolution sensitivity separately.

TargetEndpoint: Local responses to recipient demand, space, recycling and delayed effective provision
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Colony and activity observations support context. They do not select exact software feedback, timing or return rules.
MappingToCurrentParameter: Each switch selects a policy; evidence must assess behavior when enabled or disabled in defined contexts.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Use structured paired ablation contrasts with flux and task endpoints; analyze stock and transfer separately.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Feedback, supply and task ownership interact. More opportunities alone cannot resolve dose or preference.
ProposedTreatment: Retain explicit policy switches and diagnose measured response before replacing a rule.
RangeBasis: Freeze categorical policy arms; derive physical sensitivity bounds for relevant doses, groups and geometry.

TargetEndpoint: Recipient and task outcomes under alternative local access and selection policies
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Sources observe oral bouts, contacts, scouting and roles. A universal boolean decision rule has no experimental counterpart.
MappingToCurrentParameter: Controls change opportunity enumeration, eligibility or precedence; compare their downstream rates in the matching assay.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Use grouped policy ablations and event-conditioned comparisons, with transfer units preserved.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Outcome changes can reflect candidate exposure, exact deficit gating, task dwell or priority.
ProposedTreatment: Keep phase-specific settings and retain alternative controls. Use independent evidence for policy effects.
RangeBasis: Use the declared branches and observed contact windows; enforce numerical fidelity before interpreting contrasts.

TargetEndpoint: Discovery and return success, memory dependence and reversals at actual route/cue exposure
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Trajectories and choice contrasts do not expose an internal route buffer, a maximum move count or a predecessor exception.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The capped step path is a modeling construct. Search truncation can be evaluated as a sensitivity control.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Translate path steps to elapsed or physical distance with recorded resolution. Fit or compare observable decisions and failures.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Distance, timing, visibility and memory resolution all alter trip completion.
ProposedTreatment: Vary bounded approximation and use failure outcomes; choose a simpler rule if the cap remains invisible.
RangeBasis: Use observed route lengths, time to abandonment and scene dimensions, with explicit clipping and limits.

TargetEndpoint: Return path feasibility and realized work trips in the admitted initial geometry
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Construction experiments track excavation and material or group outcomes without an internal path trace.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The path is simulation state; its storage cap or inheritance has no biological estimate.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Verify path steps, travel time and physically reachable occupancy; measure discretization effects.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Observed connectivity and workers' travel influence deposit patterns independently.
ProposedTreatment: Test the bounded trace and retain numerical invariants, then compare observable actual routes.
RangeBasis: Use physical scene reach and path-resolution convergence, while holding measured substrate and inputs fixed.

TargetEndpoint: Context-specific effective detection or interaction probability versus measured distance and access
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Encounter-conditioned acceptance, care and movement do not provide a common hard radius. Known dish size is a condition.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The source has different exact distance/index/gating rules for sensing and contact. They are distinct from a sensory function.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Convert cells through physical geometry when appropriate. Measure detection with observation precision, barriers, actor state and modality.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Detection, search rate, reachability and compatible contact selection are coupled in first encounter time.
ProposedTreatment: Measure distance and exposure before bounding an effective rule. Keep multiple domain uses distinct.
RangeBasis: Use matched encounter and detection curves and physical apparatus bounds by assay, with sensitivity to spatial resolution.

TargetEndpoint: Realized travel time and movement feasibility at fixed path and load
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Observed loaded and unloaded movement constrains realized speed in separate conditions. A computational step or limit is an effective resolution setting.
MappingToCurrentParameter: Duration and segment length jointly produce movement. A global cap is an engineering safety boundary.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Compare meters/second at actual move/cadence and verify time and distance convergence.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Changing one step parameter may change speed, exposure and task dwell together.
ProposedTreatment: Treat time/space resolution and caps as controlled sensitivity. Measure actual speed separately when targeting biology.
RangeBasis: Use measured trajectories, admissible motion and invariance at finer resolution. Retain legacy numerical bounds.

TargetEndpoint: Failed searches, detection latency, repeated checks and retrieval under matched placement
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: B02 aggregate counts and markers do not resolve search pauses and unseen trajectory intervals.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The model's pause, retry budget and search geometry are proposals about movement and opportunity.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Separate detection and waiting intervals from path length and motion in a censored trajectory analysis.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Search pause, move speed, radius and unknown brood locations can produce the same elapsed time.
ProposedTreatment: Bound a simple search rule with layout sensitivity until annotated opportunities support more detail.
RangeBasis: Use apparatus geometry and observed search trajectory/time distributions. Avoid fitted retry counts from final items.

TargetEndpoint: Manipulation timing, displacement and choice opportunity as separate outcomes
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Scans and retrieval do not identify a legacy shared bout, wake interval or maximum arrangement shift.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The bounded scheduling or placement fields approximate separate measured actions.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Use timing and distance in observed units, with interval censoring and matched stage and apparatus.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Scoring cadence, true activity duration and decision cadence can produce similar positive scans.
ProposedTreatment: Range-test legacy fields; prefer measured act intervals and shifts if available.
RangeBasis: Use annotation precision, observed act frequency and physical reach; do not infer a universal work clock.

TargetEndpoint: Probability of starting or continuing care versus independently measured energy and hydration
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Worker access and tissue snapshots do not establish a fraction of simulated capacity that initiates care.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The guard applies to modeled reserves, independently of the custody gate and actual assay stimuli.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Compare conditional response by measured reserve and access with time-to-event observations.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Guard threshold, reserve initialization and maintenance change effective eligibility jointly.
ProposedTreatment: Report sensitivity to the structural guard, with measured-state response before estimating a new cutoff.
RangeBasis: Bound by ledger and observed care in documented physiological states; retain failed acts.

TargetEndpoint: Clearance, access and work opportunity with observed body/load dimensions and physical material
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Physical shape and material measurements constrain inputs. They do not set quantized box, frontier or scheduler semantics.
MappingToCurrentParameter: Algorithmic reach, wait and clearance define numerical work opportunities; effective work time and cost have separate biological endpoints.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Convert declared physical length and volume to quantized units and vary numerical resolution while holding the assay fixed.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Geometry settings alter access, work eligibility, path and deposition, so final volume alone cannot validate them.
ProposedTreatment: Run fixed-geometry fidelity and sensitivity comparisons before attributing a result to behavior.
RangeBasis: Use measured body/loads, material geometry and resolution convergence. Keep checked software limits explicit.

TargetEndpoint: Time-resolved effective uptake and delay under known dose and crop availability
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: None observes crop clearance in the target cohorts. Oral contact cadence is a different timescale.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The period sets both scheduler cadence and the effective timing of supply under the current pulse rule.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Separate numerical step from physiological latency. Compare timestamped dose/uptake series with discrete and effective continuous candidates.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Pulse timing, absorption allowance, energy yield and capacity can compensate over a terminal window.
ProposedTreatment: Treat cadence as a sensitivity factor. Constrain a biological delay only after uptake observations.
RangeBasis: Use known assay time resolution and physical time to exhaustion for sensitivity; no dose-to-body interval inferred now.

TargetEndpoint: Eligible contact opportunity and actual task-transition or waiting intervals
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Counts of bouts, exits and roles do not identify a hard sample cap, task hold or decision scheduler.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The cadence/cap determines which actors and opportunities are available, including waits.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Compare timed group/individual opportunities and transitions with software work counters kept separately.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Eligibility, event cadence, local density, task weights and interactions are coupled.
ProposedTreatment: Test interval and budget sensitivity at fixed assay conditions. Infer observable hazard or dwell only after linked observation.
RangeBasis: Derive effective exposure/time ranges from matched observations. Retain numerical caps and workload gates separately.

TargetEndpoint: Switching, depletion and stage-specific loss versus measured activity and usable reserves
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Resting respiration, actual work and cohort risk are different endpoints. They do not identify hard software thresholds.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The current guards link role and zero or fraction of stored budget to action or death.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Use matched reserves, physiological rate and competing-risk outcomes. A software zero boundary remains an accounting test.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Budget scale, initial state, uptake, role exposure and residual hazards are confounded in deaths and work totals.
ProposedTreatment: Range-test the structural assumption; consider measured activity exposure and independent risk after identifying flows.
RangeBasis: Use physically valid reserve range and measured cohort bounds. Preserve known exhaustion as a distinct event.

TargetEndpoint: Retention of private route choices at declared delay and trail context
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Route choices and experience are observed, including learning after cue removal. They do not measure a hard expiry.
MappingToCurrentParameter: A remembered coordinate list with exact lifetime is an internal rule.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Compare repeated choice error versus delay with trail and exposure controlled. Consider an observable forgetting curve.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Exact route storage, experience, delay and cue weighting can match the same choice proportions.
ProposedTreatment: Fix the current bound for comparison or replace hard expiry with a measured effective curve when identified.
RangeBasis: Use documented delay and exposure intervals. Broader memory lifetimes remain unsupported.

TargetEndpoint: Marking, behavioral dose-response and cue aging in a matched recruitment assay
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Observed mark counts and branch choices are separate. P15 estimates a 47 min behavioral e-folding time with SE 9.5 min under its fit.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The integer trail field and coefficient scale are unmeasured. An age response of choices cannot set the current scalar half-life, weight or cap.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Under the P15 exponential proxy only, half-time is 47 times ln(2) min. Use a separately defined conditional behavioral curve or physical concentration with units.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Field amplitude, response weight and thresholds can compensate. Aging and geometry affect exposure and route choices.
ProposedTreatment: Fix a reference effective scale or simplify the field before calibration. Fit aging and choices in separate contrasts with measured cue exposure.
RangeBasis: Use actual mark counts, quantified age treatments and observed response intervals. Keep the assay's effective duration and chemical decay separate.

TargetEndpoint: Turning, persistence and search/return behavior conditional on pose, experience and cue
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Trajectories and route choices are available. The shared horizontal tracks count once, and track windows are nested.
MappingToCurrentParameter: Several weights, the visited marker and initial heading choice determine the same behavioral outcome.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Use conditional transition/turn data and track hierarchy. A reduced model can set an identified reference scale.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Turning and persistence changes can trade against cue access, finite resolution and search bounds.
ProposedTreatment: Freeze a simple exploration baseline and test matched trajectories. Reduce latent weights if multiple settings remain equivalent.
RangeBasis: Use observed turning and travel contrasts, with trajectory and arena bounds. Report joint sensitivity for weights.

TargetEndpoint: Active care response over measured worker access, contact history, stage and local brood
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: B01 directly measures active scan and intervention contrasts. B02 gives retrieval counts and markers. No data resolve the modeled contact-memory law or action weights.
MappingToCurrentParameter: Scan positives combine whether an act began, how long it lasted, and its relation to inspection.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Use time-aligned active intervals, intervention and actual contacts. Compare a simple conditional probability or effective time response.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Selection, inhibition, number of opportunities, movement and act duration compensate.
ProposedTreatment: Use exposed B01 for development direction only. Fix or simplify the memory law until independent contacts and time series identify it.
RangeBasis: Bound by measured active-care response and timing, never by a fit to aggregate retrieval alone.

TargetEndpoint: Excavation initiation and continuation versus measured occupancy, local space and contact
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Group perturbations and area or CT results do not measure empty sites per contact or the software contact counts.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The current representation combines geometry, reach and local sampling; it is an engineering proxy for demand.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Measure physical void, local occupancy, contact and progression separately. Compare conditional onset with declared substrate.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Geometry and group size, sample budget and per-contact threshold affect the same removed-volume curve.
ProposedTreatment: Use bounded sensitivity or replace the proxy with an identifiable coarse feedback after measurement.
RangeBasis: Use physical space and local exposure observed in the admitted groups, with convergence at alternate resolution.

TargetEndpoint: Conditional oviposition timing and output given actual usable reserves and brood stage
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Egg and brood endpoints and tissue observations do not reveal internal attempt clocks or reserve horizons.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The current cadence schedules attempts; successful laying is separately gated. The reserve inequality is a modeling rule.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Use observation and exposure timing with interval-censored oviposition and measured reserves. Derive a reduced local hazard if data support it.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Starting reserves, uptake, depletion, per-egg debit and rejected attempts can offset each other in birth counts.
ProposedTreatment: Keep guard arms as controls. Do not infer a particular horizon from survival or optimize the software fixture.
RangeBasis: Bound candidate rules by measured reserves, inter-event times and long-term energy feasibility. Range-test existing fixed assumptions.

TargetEndpoint: Usable energy assimilation, body storage and maternal cost in a component energy balance
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Respiration, gross combustion and reproductive context do not partition available body energy and post-egg dissipation.
MappingToCurrentParameter: An effective conversion yield and reservoir capacity are model quantities. Gross chemical energy is at most a bound under stated conversion assumptions.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Compare known intake, independent oxidation/usable power and body stores over time. Preserve nJ and ug and distinguish exported energy.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Yield, initial store, activity rate, storage cap and dissipation all affect depletion. Egg or worker counts cannot identify them jointly.
ProposedTreatment: Constrain independent fluxes. If still unresolved use an explicitly fixed effective compartment or reduce the parameterization.
RangeBasis: Use chemical/physiological feasibility bounds and measured component flux uncertainty. A plausible range is not an empirical estimate.

TargetEndpoint: Larval progression as a function of acquired and retained nutrition with stage and temperature recorded
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Growth and diet treatments do not expose individual stored protein at transition. B07-X isotope evidence is congener context.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The source uses a hard tissue threshold before larval progress. A colony output or offer is not the threshold.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Compare measured individual growth and supply over time with completion and competing death.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Delivery, uptake and required tissue mass are confounded in larval completion.
ProposedTreatment: Measure growth and retention and test a simpler graded eligibility or retain the threshold as sensitivity.
RangeBasis: Use observed tissue and dose range and matched stage progression. Preserve scarcity and failures.

TargetEndpoint: Component mass in a completed positive gift conditional on contact, donor, recipient and feeding state
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Published oral events and lengths, or a meal before transfer, do not provide receiver-specific dose or a hard maximum.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The cap and default request bound an action. An attempted mass is not a committed mass.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Measure transferred components and unsuccessful bouts. Compare a conditional dose model with separate censored maxima.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Donor crop, request cap, recipient capacity and contact decisions affect realized dose together.
ProposedTreatment: Use as bounded scenario controls until dose curves or independently observed capacity identify a reduced rule.
RangeBasis: Use component availability and physiological capacity as physical limits. Derive an empirical range from measured doses.

TargetEndpoint: Recipient-specific choice or uptake given measured need, stage and compartment state
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Observed contact and whole-colony outcomes leave exact individual deficit signals, fractions and target amounts unmeasured.
MappingToCurrentParameter: Exact body/crop deficit and priority guards are proxies, not measured sensory input.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Compare conditional choice and measured component state; preserve worker/queen, delivery and absorption distinctions.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Recipient access, demand signal, selection and dose can trade off in an aggregate gift count.
ProposedTreatment: Test a simpler observable cue or fix the rule as an ablation until recipient states are measured.
RangeBasis: Use measured condition and physically possible mass ranges. Keep congener and colony output as separate constraints.

TargetEndpoint: Actual task choice and inactivity conditioned on eligible opportunities and prior task/dwell
ExistingQuantitativeEvidence: Ethograms, age/role pools and scout exposures do not identify a conditional task lottery and its scale.
MappingToCurrentParameter: The same nurse weight may act in different eligible alternatives. Marginal program residence includes travel and waiting.
UnitConversionOrStatisticalModel: Measure conditional transitions, observed act intervals and eligible alternatives. Set a reference weight in a reduced identifiable model.
CouplingAndIdentifiability: Global scaling of relative weights and eligibility, dwell and costs confound observed occupancy.
ProposedTreatment: Use fixed baseline weights or report profile sensitivity; change only the observable rule after target measurements.
RangeBasis: Use observed transition/time contrasts and explicit availability. Avoid calibrated values based on occupancy alone.
